title: Inside the stack: every token, 24 blocks
note: text = subtitles; say = spelled for the voice. Tokens from brain3d/trace.json; vectors from build/data/structure_data.json; per-block changes and head weights from build/data/blocks_data.json and heads_data.json (capture_heads.py); logit lens from trace.json logit_lens.last.

blocks.text: Emma's chat is now a row of 100 tokens. First the app's instructions, then her question. How many city e-bike battery packs do we have in Manchester stores?
blocks.say: Emma's chat is now a row of one hundred tokens. First the app's instructions, then her question. How many city e-bike battery packs do we have in Manchester stores?

blocks.text: Each token is now a column of 896 numbers. A hundred columns, side by side. This is what goes into the model.
blocks.say: Each token is now a column of eight hundred and ninety-six numbers. A hundred columns, side by side. This is what goes into the model.

blocks.text: Above them stands the stack: 24 blocks, all built the same way. Let's open the first one.
blocks.say: Above them stands the stack: twenty-four blocks, all built the same way. Let's open the first one.

blocks.text: First, attention, with 14 heads. Every position reads the positions before it, and mixes in what it needs. Battery can read city and e-bike, but never packs. Manchester can read battery. And the last position can read all 99 before it.
blocks.say: First, attention, with fourteen heads. Every position reads the positions before it, and mixes in what it needs. Battery can read city and e-bike, but never packs. Manchester can read battery. And the last position can read all ninety-nine before it.

blocks.text: Then the MLP. It takes each column on its own, widens it from 896 numbers to 4,864, and squeezes it back to 896. Here, no column sees any other.
blocks.say: Then the MLP. It takes each column on its own, widens it from eight hundred and ninety-six numbers to four thousand eight hundred and sixty-four, and squeezes it back to eight hundred and ninety-six. Here, no column sees any other.

blocks.text: Out come 100 columns, and every one of them has changed. Then all 100 climb to the next block, and it happens again. And again. All the way through block 24.
blocks.say: Out come one hundred columns, and every one of them has changed. Then all one hundred climb to the next block, and it happens again. And again. All the way through block twenty-four.

blocks.text: At the top, the model reads out just one column: the last one. Only its 896 numbers are turned into scores for the next token.
blocks.say: At the top, the model reads out just one column: the last one. Only its eight hundred and ninety-six numbers are turned into scores for the next token.

blocks.text: So why work on the other 99? Because in every block, the last position reads them. That is how Emma's words reach the answer. In block 24, one head puts 65 percent of its weight on Manchester. In block 19, another reads stores. Without those columns, there would be nothing to read.
blocks.say: So why work on the other ninety-nine? Because in every block, the last position reads them. That is how Emma's words reach the answer. In block twenty-four, one head puts sixty-five percent of its weight on Manchester. In block nineteen, another reads stores. Without those columns, there would be nothing to read.

blocks.text: Can we watch the answer form? Ask the last column early, after each block: what would you say now? For 17 blocks, noise. At block 18, a lowercase we. From block 22, We leads: 8 percent, then 29, then 56.
blocks.say: Can we watch the answer form? Ask the last column early, after each block: what would you say now? For seventeen blocks, noise. At block eighteen, a lowercase we. From block twenty-two, We leads: eight percent, then twenty-nine, then fifty-six.

blocks.text: Every block reads the row with 14 heads. Next: what each of those heads looks for.
blocks.say: Every block reads the row with fourteen heads. Next: what each of those heads looks for.
